statements.text: I, too, am concerned that the cost of energy is going to rise for a community that already suffers from one of the highest rates of poverty in the state of California. I’m concerned about the effects of data centers on the grid, where the risk of blackouts will go up, and people will be more frequently without power in the desert heat, and vulnerable populations are going to be at risk of heat illness.
statements.venue: Instagram video message, as reported by Imperial Valley Press

statements.text: We’d like to send a very clear message that I unequivocally oppose the proposed data center in the city of Coachella. It raises costs. It would worsen the health of, especially our vulnerable populations and for the neighborhoods living near there.
statements.venue: Statement to Coachella City Council (reported by AICV News)

statements.text: I unequivocally oppose data centers in Imperial Valley and urge local officials to prevent them from happening. The data is clear. Data centers in their current form and near neighborhoods reduce life expectancy, pollute the air, worsen asthma rates, increase energy costs and require more water than we can afford. There is also concern regarding the impact of a heat dome on vulnerable people and the mental health effect of constant noise pollution.
statements.venue: Statement read into Imperial County Board of Supervisors record (reported by The Desert Review)

statements.text: Right now, the incentives are unbalanced: companies get the economic benefit while communities absorb the water use, noise, pollution and energy grid strain. Congress should require federal environmental review and community disclosure for data centers seeking federal incentives or connecting to federally regulated transmission, set water- and energy-efficiency standards tied to any federal support, and ensure local governments and tribes have real consultation rights before permitting. [...] The U.S. can lead in AI and cloud computing, but that leadership has to be built on sustainable siting decisions, not on risking the health of people who live near them or using limited water resources increasing energy costs, worsening health through pollution, noise, and heat dome effects.
statements.venue: Southern California News Group / Press Enterprise 2026 candidate questionnaire

statements.text: I support strict, enforceable disclosure requirements: any political ad using AI-generated or manipulated audio, video, or images of a real person should carry a clear, conspicuous label, and materially deceptive deepfakes of a candidate, content designed to make a person appear to say or do something they didn’t, should be prohibited outright, with a real enforcement mechanism at the FEC. [...] This is exactly the kind of issue where Congress needs to legislate ahead of the technology instead of reacting after an election has already been affected.
statements.venue: Southern California News Group / Press Enterprise 2026 candidate questionnaire
